images.title: Four straight sides, four angles
images.purpose: Shows what makes a figure a quadrilateral: a closed shape of exactly four straight sides with one angle at each corner.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large irregular four sided shape in the centre, its sides and its corner angles picked out in two colours.
images.exact_structure: One convex irregular quadrilateral ABCD filling about half the frame height, no two sides parallel and no right angles. Its four straight sides are drawn as thick teal (#0072B2) lines that meet only at their ends, so the shape is closed. At each of the four corners a small filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) angle arc sits inside the shape, exactly four arcs. The capital letters A, B, C and D sit just outside the four corners, going round in order. To the right of the shape, the label 4 sides in teal and, under it, the label 4 angles in reddish purple. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A quadrilateral is a closed figure with four straight sides and four angles.
images.description: Shows what makes a figure a quadrilateral: a closed shape of exactly four straight sides with one angle at each corner.
images.context: Chapter opening: the definition of a quadrilateral, its sides and its angles.

image_decisions.why: A single clean quadrilateral with its four sides and four angles marked shows exactly what the word means.
